newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela unfazed by privatization opposition.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela unfazed by privatization opposition.

text.p: The Venezuelan government is not concerned by recent protests at home that its planned privatization program will sell off state assets on the cheap, Planning Minister Teodoro Petkoff said Friday.
"Whatever the price...there will always be people in Venezuela saying that they are being sold cheaply," Petkoff told Reuters in a brief telephone interview.

"It's a recurrent theme in Venezuelan politics...It's inevitable," he said, after calling Reuters to reiterate a denial that he was planning to resign or that President Rafael Caldera was planning on shaking up his cabinet of ministers.
Local politicians have began to criticize government privatization plans in recent weeks urging that strong efforts be made to maximize any sale prices.

Opposition has been strongest in the case of telephone CANTV where politicians have insisted that the sale price for a planned global issue of 40 percent of the company in mid November should not fall below the $4.71 per share price obtained for 40 percent of the company in 1991.

Petkoff stressed that it would be the market which sets the price of the CANTV share issue and added that arguments over price represented "a debate between the Venezuela which wants to modernize and the dinosaurs."
Petkoff also dismissed as "ridiculous" a largely pacific demonstration in the capital Thursday night against the rising cost of living.
The organized pot banging and fireworks on Thursday were part of "our urban landscape" which includes frequent small-scale clashes between students and police, Petkoff said.
